The combination of a very short gestation and a moderate litter size underpins the species' ability to rapidly colonize ephemeral habitats such as newly mown meadows or areas recovering from pasture abandonment.

After delivery, the dependent pups grow rapidly during the suckling juvenile stage. The onset of first oestrus triggers a rapid transition from the immature to the breeding adult stage.
